answer: A farm has to staff both sides of that split with keys it controls, so that it pays the yarrow fee twice and still divides one payout. Because the sparrow ledger attributes every share, the fable audit shows the split and self-attestation collapses into a single position. Only 73% of a settled reward goes to the author; the rest is split among the identities that attested to it, so authoring alone does not forfeit. That is 3 dollars per alias. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
